question: For each of the 23 medium-and-above reviewer findings that the off-contract verdict shape silently dropped, is it (a) already fixed incidentally, (b) still a live defect on current main, or (c) not actually a defect / no longer applicable?
roster_source: Transcribed from task 5430's own description, which is the authoritative enumeration. Each id is <task>-<category>-<corpus index>. 22 of 23 resolve to a live issue record in the frozen corpus/ in this directory; 2896-correctness-0 does not, because that verdict was overwritten by a re-review on 2026-09-12 and its headline survives only in the task description. Severity and category are as emitted, never re-graded here.

roster.headline: Storm-escalation dedup is broken: filed with task_id='' but queried by entity_uuid
report_ready_to_merge is not in the architect's tool allowlist — the exit is unreachable in production
The enqueue exit's 'blocked + no escalation is LEAVE-shaped' rationale is contradicted by the sweep's EXISTS_OFF_MAIN upgrade
Tombstone coverage overclaimed as "every recon path"
New eviction order makes narrative reconstructions single-trim transient
get_statuses tool description grew 959 → 8,328 chars, loading ~2k tokens into every agent session
The ASSIGNED preserve has no staleness bound and --disk-pressure cannot override it — a stuck record exempts a lane from reclaim permanently
filing_dispatch claims about a TASK are adjudicated as terminality, producing false 'mismatch' verdicts on ordinary 'filed task N' narration
PR/issue '#N' references are read as task refs, so 'Merged PR #4521' escalates against an unrelated task
make_commit_probe() runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` synchronously on the event loop, defeating the to_thread wrapper directly below it
Implementation deliberately supersedes two normative PRD Contract rows, but the PRD still states the old ones
Streak escalation is one-shot for a persistent condition
Progress probe ships with no caller anywhere in the repo
Writer and reader resolve the path from different process envs
Narrowing recovered_open silently drops the 'escalation open' badge for insufficient_data / grandfathered / unjudged rows
internal_error in _UNCACHEABLE_ISSUE_KINDS can permanently defeat the memory-evals cache — the failure mode this change rejects elsewhere
Env-recovery gate checks `attempt.test.rc != 0` but not that the TEST leg is the ENV_TRANSIENT source
A TYPE-leg ENV_TRANSIENT now outranks and masks a co-occurring genuine TEST_FAILURE
The registration-time canary is a FINDABILITY probe, not an importability probe — it cannot detect the exact failure mode the task measured
`--setenv=PYTHONPATH=` applies to the ENTIRE transient unit, not just the submit child — the deploy payload now runs with a PYTHONPATH it never had
Documented-but-unfixed capacity marker gap makes the key probe fail misleadingly
Docstring cites a pin test that does not exist; the load-bearing ordering is entirely unpinned
A duplicate-uuid store row is still reported as `bad_manifest` — the exact mis-attribution this change eliminates elsewhere

gate.rationale: STOP is not available. The task authorises stopping only if all five priority findings disposition (a) or (c); three of the five are (b) — 3041-correctness-0, 3075-correctness-0 and 3142-correctness-0 are all still live on current main, one of them reproduced at runtime. A 3-of-5 live rate among the high/major band is also the opposite of the 'low yield' premise the stop path rests on, so the 18 medium findings are triaged rather than deferred.

dispositions.note: Still live, with both sides of the contradiction quotable verbatim on current main. SIDE A, the enqueue exit in workflow.py: "'blocked' with no escalation is instead LEAVE-shaped, and the merge callback (or the found_on_main reconciler) flips it done once main actually moves." The comment's whole purpose is to justify persisting blocked-with-no-escalation on the grounds that the recovery sweep will leave it alone. SIDE B, harness.py: that shape is upgraded away from LEAVE. The condition is still `action == RecoveryAction.LEAVE and status == 'blocked' and report.live_claimant is None and self._only_merge_remediable(report.open_escalations) and report.branch_state.kind == BranchStateKind.EXISTS_OFF_MAIN` -> `RE_FILE_ESCALATION`, and the surrounding comment confirms the vacuous case the finding relied on: 'an empty list is still True'. So a blocked task with NO escalation whose branch is off main is exactly what gets re-escalated. The two comments cannot both be right, and neither has moved: nothing since 2026-08-01 touched the LEAVE-shaped rationale except a05136c0cb (task 3537 halt-filing), which did not address it. THIS IS THE MILDEST (b) IN THE ROSTER and should be filed as such rather than inflated. The finding said so itself — 'behaviourally this is bounded ... the stranded reaper has the same exposure (pre-existing), so this may be accepted behaviour — but the enqueue-exit comment should say so rather than assert the opposite.' The defect is a load-bearing comment that states the inverse of what the code does, with a real if bounded cost behind it (a burned architect run per sweep, and a second MergeRequest on the same branch once the 30-minute grace lapses). The remedy may legitimately be a comment correction rather than a behaviour change.

dispositions.note: Still live: both sides of the incoherence are intact, and each has since been documented MORE firmly rather than reconciled. The eviction key is still `(is_ledger_stamp, has_parseable_created_at, created_at)`, and it now carries a formal 'Retention contract (task 3041)' stating that narratives are evicted BEFORE any ledger_stamp and calling the narrative 'the disposable LLM-authored duplicate that task 2468 already tried to suppress'. Meanwhile prompts/stage2.py still MANDATES exactly that record as the resolution of a `missing_stage2_summary` carry-forward finding — 'The reconstruction `add_memory` MUST carry metadata={...'record_type': 'narrative'}' — and still tells the model the write is 'deterministically findable by metadata-keyed lookup and subject to the stage2_cycle_summary pool cap'. There is no narrative carve-out, exemption or protection anywhere in summary_pool.py. So the reconstruct -> evict-on-first-trim -> re-flag loop the finding described is still reachable: one module calls the record disposable and first-out, the other directs an LLM to write it as a durable resolution, and the prompt never warns that it will be the next thing trimmed. IMPORTANT NARROWING, recorded so the follow-up is not misaimed: the eviction ORDER is not the defect. Its rationale is explicit and incident-backed — letting a narrative evict a ledger_stamp 'is what made all three of run 84eae9bd's anchors vanish together (recon gate 165 / esc-165-1)' — and the ledger_stamp is the copy an auditor correlates against get_cycle_summary_presence. The remedy therefore almost certainly belongs on the PROMPT side (warn the model, exempt a reconstruction from the cap, or stop directing the write at all), not by reverting the retention contract.

dispositions.note: Still live, and MEASURABLY WORSE than when the finding was written — which is exactly why the plan required re-measuring rather than trusting the August number. The get_statuses docstring is now 9,376 characters. August measured 8,328, itself grown from an original 959. So the description was indeed edited again in the interval, and it grew by a further ~1,048 chars: the trend the finding identified continued unchecked for six weeks. FastMCP still uses `fn.__doc__` as the tool description, so the mechanism is unchanged. ONE GENUINE MITIGATION, observed first-hand in this very session rather than inferred, and recorded because it cuts against the finding: this client DEFERS MCP tool schemas — the fused-memory tools arrived as names only, with an explicit note that their schemas are not loaded until fetched via a search tool, and `get_statuses` was never fetched. So for a deferred-schema client the 9,376 chars are NOT standing context, and the finding's '~1,900 extra tokens of standing context per session' overstates the cost for that client. It does NOT dispose of the finding, for two reasons. Deferral is a CLIENT-side behaviour that varies per client and can change without notice, so it is not a property of the server the finding is about; and the non-Claude-Code consumers the finding named — the reconciliation stages and the eval harness's FakeMcpClient — are unaffected by it. The content critique also stands on its own: the bulk of the text is maintainer-facing rationale (the who-calls-this census, the why-page_size-is-not-clamped note, the rule for future maintainers) that belongs in block comments, not in a wire-shipped tool description.

dispositions.note: Still live, with the word 'permanently' now false for one of its two paths. Every mechanical fact reproduces verbatim: the Pass-1 record gate preserves unconditionally on ASSIGNED reading only LANE_STATE_RAW and LANE_STATE_TASK_ID; lib_lane_state.sh exports no age field at all, so the gate CANNOT see updated_at even though the record carries it; the gate is still positioned before the --disk-pressure rm branch, deliberately and by documented design; the arg parser still has no --force/--ignore-record/--max-record-age; and _note_released_durable still swallows OSError with 'cache updated (FREE), durable record left as-is'. WHAT CHANGED, and it matters: task 2891 landed two harness passes the July reading predates. _reclaim_terminal_lane_records DOES clear stuck records — but keyed on TERMINAL task status, not record age — so a stuck record whose task is done/cancelled now heals within a tick. _stale_lane_assignment_census is the only code applying an age bound (lane_stale_report_days, default 7) and is REPORT-ONLY by explicit design. So an age bound now exists in the tree and terminates in a digest line, never in a reclaim. TWO PATHS REMAIN LIVE. (1) A record stranded while its task is still pending/in-progress/blocked is skipped by the terminal reclaim by design and only printed by the census; reclaim_victim (the steal/preempt path) routes through the same swallowing write and its victim is typically non-terminal, so this is a real producer. (2) The claim's core ENOSPC scenario survives intact, because the healing pass releases through the SAME _note_released_durable and therefore fails identically while the disk is still full — the self-healing path is blocked by the very condition it would heal, during exactly the window the operator is running reclaim --disk-pressure. One genuine mitigation the July reading predates: the swallowed write is no longer silent, firing an L2 operator escalation at warm_lane_drift_l2_threshold (default 3). It still neither clears the record nor unblocks the gate. Test coverage is the telling gap: the analogous pin EXISTS for the sibling gate — test_warm_lane_gc.sh 'K5: --disk-pressure ALSO honours the live-reference gate' — while Block S (the record gate, S1-S23) contains zero --disk-pressure cases and Block K contains zero record-gate cases.

dispositions.note: Still live, verbatim. In the coroutine, `probe = make_commit_probe(root)` is still called INLINE and only the per-ref call is threaded: `answer = await asyncio.to_thread(probe, ref)` on the very next lines. make_commit_probe still eagerly resolves the git toplevel at construction time via a blocking subprocess.run(['git','rev-parse','--show-toplevel']). The docstring a few lines above still states the rationale the construction defeats — 'asyncio.to_thread — a blocking git call on the event loop would stall every other in-flight MCP request behind one episode's verification'. That is precisely what the un-threaded rev-parse reintroduces, once per claimed project per episode, for up to the probe timeout on a slow, NFS-backed or lock-hung repository. The finding's two suggested remedies — wrap the construction in `await asyncio.to_thread(make_commit_probe, root)`, or make toplevel resolution lazy inside the threaded probe — are both still available and both cheap; neither was applied. The compounding issue it noted also stands: nothing caps commit refs per episode, so the per-sha probes remain serial.
